mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 700K units, indicating strong demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 700K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, a strong labor market signals economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when UNRATE < 6% and PAYEMS growth > 200K, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals reduced supply chain pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as input costs decrease.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns after INDPRO declines > 2% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real disposable personal income (RSAFS) grows by more than 5% in a month, increased consumer spending boosts economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when RSAFS growth > 5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 8% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) shrinks by more than 100K in a month, a weak labor market signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 40% of instances when UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS decline > 100K, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 3% in a quarter signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as increased economic activity boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when GDPC1 growth > 3% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
